solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: Television screening one old ruler born on a fasting day

indicators.note: a screen hides what is behind it, so the outer word wraps around the pieces that follow

parts.note: TV is the usual short form of television

indicators.note: 'on' here means placed right next to, so the next item follows directly

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
the title of the former monarchs of Iran
b. is the abbreviation for born in biographies
taken as written

explanation.surface: A television programme shows an elderly monarch whose birthday falls on a day of fasting.
explanation.walkthrough: The outer TV holds the whole run I + SHAH + B + A, giving Tishah b'Av.
explanation.definitionFit: Tishah b'Av, the ninth of the month Av, is the Jewish day of fasting that mourns the destruction of the Temples.

clue.text: Merchant advanced weird notion

parts.note: A is the standard abbreviation for advanced, as in A level

indicators.note: something weird is strange or out of shape, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A trader puts forward a strange idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Merchant' with a capital hides a literary title: Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio is the title character of Shakespeare's play The Merchant of Venice, the man who borrows from Shylock.

clue.text: Pole set on getting grass in Glasgow

parts.note: S for the south pole
an old verb tar meant to incite or set on, as dogs are set on a quarry

explanation.surface: A Polish person is attacked for being on the grass in a Scottish city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a nationality, but it is a compass point. The verb tar in 'tar on' is an obsolete word for urging dogs to attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Star or starr is a Scots word for sedge or coarse bent grass, so it is grass as a Scot would name it.

clue.text: Dee for example, New Age choir leader in Perth?

parts.note: Dee is the spelt-out name of the letter D

indicators.note: something new is made over, so the letters of the next word are freshly arranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A river in Scotland is given as an example, next to a New Age choirmaster in a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a Scottish river, which fits Perth, but here Dee is just how you spell the name of the letter D.
explanation.definitionFit: A lettergae is the Scots name for a precentor, who leads the singing in church; Perth signals a Scottish word.

clue.text: Bank on upset after mixture with no little Bass

indicators.note: 'after' places the upturned word behind the other piece
'with no' says the following item has to be taken away

parts.note: a blend is a mixture
B is the abbreviation for bass in music

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the short word is read the other way

parts.note: re means on, about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone bets on an upset result after a blend without much bass in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks like a verb going with 'on', as in rely on, but it is the noun; 'on' is the separate word meaning about.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank is an institution that lends money, so it is a lender.

clue.text: Old Russian in dire straits

indicators.note: something in a dire state is a mess, so the following word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A Russian of the old days is in terrible trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarist was a supporter of the tsars, so the word fits a Russian of the old imperial era.

clue.text: Pressing General during leave

indicators.note: 'during' puts one thing in the middle of another's span, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to exit is to leave
Gen. is the abbreviation for General

explanation.surface: An army general is pressing to be dealt with while on leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave' looks like a soldier's holiday, but it is a verb meaning go out.
explanation.definitionFit: Exigent means urgent or demanding immediate attention, which is what a pressing matter is.

clue.text: No lead in pencil? That's material!

indicators.note: with no lead the word loses its opening letter, the one at the front

parts.note: a crayon is a coloured pencil

explanation.surface: A pencil with no lead in it: how useless is that!
explanation.walkthrough: The 'lead' of a pencil is the graphite core in the surface, but here it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rayon is an artificial silk fabric, a cloth or material made from cellulose.

clue.text: Looks to hedge pound leading to complaint

indicators.note: a hedge surrounds a field, so the outer word encloses the next piece

parts.note: a gander is a look, as in 'take a gander'
L is the symbol for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone peers at a hedge round an animal pound, which leads to a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Glanders is a contagious disease of horses, and complaint is a common word for an illness.

clue.text: Car's first for outstanding sound

parts.note: Audi is a German make of car

indicators.note: 'first' asks for only the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: the opening letter of outstanding

explanation.surface: A car's top feature is its excellent sound system.
explanation.walkthrough: The make of car comes first, then just the first letter of 'outstanding'.
explanation.definitionFit: Audio means relating to sound, and is used as a noun for recorded or transmitted sound.

clue.text: During brief kiss, one's showing male and female characteristics

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'
terse means brief or curt
X stands for a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: During a quick kiss, a person shows traits of both sexes.
explanation.definitionFit: Intersex describes a person or animal with sexual characteristics intermediate between male and female.

clue.text: Lily has a change of direction in compound

indicators.note: a change of direction swaps right for left, so one direction letter is swapped for the other

parts.note: the arum lily, often just called arum

explanation.surface: A lily turns another way inside a walled compound.
explanation.walkthrough: R stands for right and L for left, so changing direction turns the R into an L.
explanation.definitionFit: Alum is a chemical compound, a double sulphate of aluminium and potassium used in dyeing.

clue.text: Verse and German dance boring French company

indicators.note: to bore is to drill into something, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: SA, société anonyme, is the French equivalent of Ltd or Inc
Tanz is the German word for dance

explanation.surface: Poetry and a German dance turn out to be tedious for a French firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' reads as dull, but it means drilling into.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanza is a group of lines forming a unit of a poem, so it is a verse.

clue.text: Capital invested originally in Hardy hit

indicators.note: something hit is knocked about, so these letters are thrown into a new order
'originally' means at the start, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter of invested
the name supplies letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Money originally invested in a Hardy novel became a hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests money, which the word invested strengthens, but it means a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Riyadh is the capital city of Saudi Arabia.

clue.text: Wandering tribe, debauched by the sound of it

indicators.note: the phrase tells you to go by how a word is spoken, not how it is written

parts.note: whored means debauched, consorted with prostitutes

explanation.surface: A nomadic tribe has, it seems, a reputation for debauchery.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech the r is silent and the w unspoken, so the two words sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A horde was originally a tribe of nomadic Tartars or other wandering people.

clue.text: Rob mostly after a shot making no angle

indicators.note: 'mostly' means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter
'after' puts the shortened word behind the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
a go is a shot or attempt
to nick is to steal or rob

explanation.surface: A thief nearly takes a shot but gets the angle wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Agonic, from Greek a- not and gonia angle, means having or making no angle, as in the agonic line of zero magnetic declination.

clue.text: Walton's advice perhaps succeeded for some of the percussion

parts.note: Izaak Walton wrote The Compleat Angler, so his advice might be to cast a net
s. is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: A composer's tip turned out well for the percussion section.
explanation.walkthrough: Walton suggests the composer William Walton and an orchestral setting, but it is Izaak Walton, the 17th-century writer on fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Castanets are a pair of clicking shells played in the hand, so they form part of the percussion.

clue.text: Innocent Ealing comedy's number one for broadcasting

indicators.note: broadcasting scatters things widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: number one means the first, so only the word's opening letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter of comedy

explanation.surface: An innocent Ealing comedy is the top choice for television.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ealing comedies were gentle British films of the 1940s and 50s made at Ealing Studios in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Angelic means like an angel, pure and innocent.

clue.text: Sweetener from corrupt clergy leads to local order

indicators.note: something corrupt is spoiled from its proper form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: the leads of words are their front letters, so only the first of each is taken

parts.note: the opening letters of local and order

explanation.surface: Bribes from crooked clergy bring about a local religious order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetener' suggests a bribe in the surface, but it is a literal sweet substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Glycerol, also called glycerine, is a sweet-tasting syrupy liquid used as a sweetening agent in food.

clue.text: Take tea crossing motorway in unconventional region

indicators.note: to cross something here is to stretch over it, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: bohea is a black China tea
the M1, written with I for one, is Britain's main north-south motorway

explanation.surface: Someone takes tea on the way over a motorway, somewhere out of the ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: Bohea is an old name for black tea, and the M1 runs from London to Leeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Bohemia is a region of the Czech Republic and also a name for the community of unconventional artists and writers.

clue.text: Virtuous son going out more!

parts.note: s. is the abbreviation for son
someone going out more is staying in less

explanation.surface: A well-behaved son is allowed out more often!
explanation.walkthrough: The second part is a cryptic paraphrase: going out more means being in less, read as the two words IN LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinless means free from sin, which is to be morally good or virtuous.

clue.text: Parrot learned after scratching head

indicators.note: scratching out the head removes the word's first letter

parts.note: literate means learned, well read

explanation.surface: A parrot learned its words after scratching its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parrot' looks like the bird, but it is the verb meaning to say again.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to repeat words mechanically, and to iterate is to say or do again.

clue.text: S African dish provided by very French composer

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so good'
Erik Satie, French composer of the Gymnopédies

explanation.surface: A South African meal was provided by an extremely French composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sosatie is a South African kebab of curried or spiced meat grilled on a skewer.

clue.text: Refuse to co-operate with sporting Knight

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to shun or refuse to deal with
second meaning: Sir Geoffrey, the knighted Yorkshire and England cricketer

explanation.surface: A sportsman refuses to work with a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: Geoffrey Boycott was an opening batsman for England, knighted in 2019.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to refuse dealings with someone in protest, and the surname belongs to a famous cricketing knight.

clue.text: School dormitory, Dom expelled for wild behaviour

indicators.note: to school is to train and reshape, so the remaining letters are put into new order
someone expelled is thrown out, so these letters are taken away

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, letters to be removed

explanation.surface: A monk is thrown out of a school dormitory for bad behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' looks like a noun for where the dormitory is, but it is a verb. The D, O and M come out separately, leaving RITORY to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Riotry is an old word for riotous conduct, which is wild, disorderly behaviour.

clue.text: Heard clergyman in processed food outlets

indicators.note: heard means the word is taken by its spoken form, not its spelling

parts.note: a rector is a parish clergyman

explanation.surface: A vicar was overheard in a fast-food shop.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech the final r of rector is silent. 'Food outlets' reads as shops, but it is anatomical.
explanation.definitionFit: The rectum, plural recta, is the last part of the gut, the exit for food once digested.

clue.text: Hard in centre of clubland to get a dance for oldies

indicators.note: 'in' puts the first piece inside the second
'centre of' asks for only the middle letters of the next word

parts.note: the two middle letters of clubland
raw means harsh or hard, as in a raw deal

explanation.surface: Older people find it hard to get a dance in the heart of the nightclub scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The key printed CRAWL, but the wordplay gives BRAWL, as the solving blog later confirmed. 'For oldies' marks an archaic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A brawl was an old French round dance, the branle, so the word names a dance from past centuries.

clue.text: Priest featured in writing by a girl

indicators.note: 'by' means beside, so the last piece goes next to the rest
something featured in a piece appears inside it, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: MSS is the abbreviation for manuscripts, pieces of writing
Eli is the priest in the Bible who raised Samuel
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clergyman appears in a piece written by a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Melissa is a girl's name, from the Greek for honeybee.

clue.text: Paid out before vehicle duty sent round

indicators.note: sent round means put around something, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: VED, Vehicle Excise Duty, is the UK's annual road tax
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Someone paid before the car tax was sent around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paid out' suggests spending money, but it is the sailor's sense of letting out a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: To veer a rope or cable is to let it out or pay it out gradually, a nautical sense.

clue.text: Head certainly returned old gold coin

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: nab is a slang word for the head
OK means certainly, all right

explanation.surface: The head of the mint certainly sent back an old gold coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The koban was an oblong gold coin of feudal Japan.

clue.text: Sponge filling initially bog standard stuff

parts.note: to bum is to sponge or cadge

indicators.note: 'initially' means at the start, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of filling

explanation.surface: A sponge filling is nothing special.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sponge' looks like cake, the filling its jam, but it is the verb to cadge. Bog is British slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumf, short for bum-fodder, is slang for toilet paper and so for routine papers, the standard stuff of a lavatory.

clue.text: Leave bedbug and scratch!

parts.note: scram is slang for leave quickly
B is slang for a bedbug, from B flat

explanation.surface: Get out of bed, bitten by bugs, and have a scratch!
explanation.definitionFit: Scramb is a dialect verb meaning to scratch with the nails or claws.

clue.text: Shrewd piecework in HQ, billions spent

indicators.note: something spent is used up and gone, so these letters disappear
'in' places the first piece inside the second

parts.note: a headquarters is a base
tut is a dialect word for piecework, paid by the job
b is the abbreviation for billion

explanation.surface: Paying by the piece at head office, with billions spent, looks shrewd.
explanation.walkthrough: Tut is an old dialect word for work paid by the piece rather than by the hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Astute means clever at judging situations to one's advantage, which is shrewd.

clue.text: Broadcast admitting tare in Scottish crop

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the outer word takes the other inside

parts.note: to broadcast seed is to sow it by scattering
t is the abbreviation for tare, the weight of packaging

explanation.surface: Seed sown by hand lets in tares among a Scottish harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crop' looks like a noun for the harvest, but it is the verb to cut short. Tare is also a weed, which feeds the farming picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Stow is a Scots verb meaning to crop or lop off, so it is a Scottish word for crop.

clue.text: Call in popular Italian and stop for a bit

indicators.note: 'in' places the first piece inside the pair that follows

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
to term is to call or name
It is the abbreviation for Italian, as in It vermouth

explanation.surface: A popular Italian phones in and stays a while.
explanation.definitionFit: To intermit is to suspend or stop something temporarily, so it is to pause for a time.

clue.text: Note Liberal really upset — it's trifling stuff

parts.note: fa is a note in the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A note says a Liberal is really cross, though it is only a trivial matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Fallalery means fallals collectively, showy trifles and frippery, so it is trivial finery.
